For the open discussion, if there is time: three data points for the lifetime question (2^24 or 2^30).

1. **Both candidates on a microcontroller, measured.** I ran leanVM's signer (`crates/lean_sphincs` at a0fa68a; for 2^24 with the constants from sphincs.art: heights 10 + 7 + 7, k = 19, a = 9) on an ESP32 at 240 MHz: one core, Keccak in software, the top tree's leaves kept (16 KiB). Eight signatures averaged 15.2 s at 2^24 and 28.5 s at 2^30. At the mean count over 1,000 messages (142K and 256K permutations) that is about 17 s against 30 s. A key takes about 30 s (271K permutations). At the Nano S+ rate from Tom's benchmark (5.8K per second) the same counts give 24 s against 44 s, close to sphincs.art.

2. **One-time keys on the same board.** A WOTS signature takes 0.3 s. In my prototype the stateless key certifies a tree of one-time keys and those sign the transactions, so the board pays the stateless time once per tree, not per transaction.

3. **The budget after a restore.** A key that is derived from a recovery phrase comes back without its signature count, and every device that holds the phrase draws on the same budget. ERC-8499 (hash-based key derivation from BIP-39) had to write rules for this; the lifetime decides how much room such a key has.

Code and log: https://github.com/johba37/winterlock.eth/tree/dd36a89d6bdac208d1962597229f1ef2648e0eef/hardware/esp32-leansphincs-bench
Other board measurements: https://github.com/johba37/winterlock.eth/blob/main/docs/findings.md#signing-times
ERC-8499: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8499-hash-based-key-derivation-from-bip-39/30375
